headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate or misuse content via broad network/MCP while LightZero has no shared channel, so prompt-injection and leakage risks are mostly one-sided but still material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot ingest next-ai-draw-io output automatically. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer into next-ai-draw-io’s natural-language/MCP workflow, which is a weak prompt-injection path. This is lower risk because the pair lacks a default shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LightZero-generated text into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to treat imported text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of prompt fields; paste only into labeled data fields.
Use a fixed instruction template that separates data from directives.
Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary text when processing LightZero artifacts.
Review imported text for instruction-like phrases before submission.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, but next-ai-draw-io handles files and sends requests to multiple external AI APIs by default. If LightZero artifacts are copied into next-ai-draw-io, those contents can leave the local environment. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path once the two are used together.
conditions: IF LightZero-generated artifacts are pasted or uploaded into next-ai-draw-io, their contents may be transmitted to third-party model APIs.
IF next-ai-draw-io is run with external API providers enabled, file contents can leave the host.
mitigations: Use local-only models in next-ai-draw-io for LightZero artifacts.
Redact secrets before importing any LightZero output.
Restrict next-ai-draw-io to a dedicated workspace with non-sensitive files.
Turn off external API providers for sessions that process LightZero content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or use the network, so it has no mutable-resource overlap with next-ai-draw-io. next-ai-draw-io can support multiple instances, but without any write capability on LightZero there is no shared-write conflict to arbitrate. The pathway is therefore blocked by profile facts.
conditions: IF LightZero gains filesystem or git write capability in a future deployment, shared-resource conflicts could emerge.
IF next-ai-draw-io is paired with a different writable agent, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Avoid co-locating writable agents in the same workspace.
Document any future write-capable integration before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero does not expose outputs to next-ai-draw-io by default, so there is no automatic authority chain. Any cascade requires manual transfer of LightZero text into next-ai-draw-io, where it may be rendered into diagrams or AI-assisted content. That makes the pathway possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the produced document.
conditions: IF LightZero output is manually used as source material for next-ai-draw-io diagrams, errors can propagate into the final document.
IF next-ai-draw-io is used without a human verification step, incorrect content may be rendered as authoritative.
mitigations: Require human review before importing LightZero-derived text.
Annotate imported content as unverified source material.
Use a checklist to verify any facts before diagram generation.
Keep generated diagrams separate from source notes.

E_compliance.rationale: LightZero is open-source game-playing software with no touched data classes, while next-ai-draw-io handles files and API keys and may send content to external AI providers. If the operator uses regulated or sensitive documents in next-ai-draw-io, residency and retention obligations can be violated even though LightZero itself is not the compliance driver. The mismatch is on the document-processing side.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed in next-ai-draw-io, external API routing may create residency or retention issues.
IF API keys are configured for third-party providers, compliance obligations extend beyond local processing.
mitigations: Process only non-sensitive documents in next-ai-draw-io.
Prefer local models for regulated content.
Review provider retention terms before uploading files.
Separate API keys by environment and purpose.
